title: How tall is a stronger wave?
hook: Change wave intensity and predict wave amplitude.
misconception: wave amplitude doubles when wave intensity doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply A ∝ √I to compare wave amplitude when wave intensity changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a linear wave with fixed frequency medium and other parameters, A ∝ √I. When wave intensity doubles, wave amplitude becomes √2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model A ∝ √I; scaling exponent 0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a linear wave with fixed frequency medium and other parameters, with a nonzero initial result. If wave intensity triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on wave amplitude?
recall.why: Apply A ∝ √I under the same assumptions: the multiplier is √3.
